name_story.story: Abram can be understood through the Arabic form إبراهيم, whose central sense is exalted father. faq.a: Abram is associated with the Arabic form إبراهيم, whose core sense is exalted father.

faq.q: What is the origin of Abram?
faq.a: Abram is associated with Arabic. Abram is the Hebrew biblical form (אַבְרָם, 'exalted father'); the Arabic Qur'anic form is إبراهيم (Ibrāhīm). The two are related but not identical, and the source record conflated them.
Yes — the underlying form إبراهيم is Arabic.
Abram can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Abram should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. إبراهيم is the Qur'anic form of the prophet's name

faq.a: Romanization variants include Abram, abram. Script forms are إبراهيم, ابراهيم, ابراہیم, इब्राहीम.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
